# A module is completed whole, so a build that imports several of its packages
# needs no second pass, whichever of them it happened to load first.
#
# One package of this module has a directive that fails on purpose. A module
# whose generator failed is incomplete, and handing it over breaks the build
# later at an undefined symbol. So the fetch fails and names the package whose
# generator failed.

env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod

! go mod download example.com/generatedpkgs
stderr 'generating example.com/generatedpkgs'
stderr 'in broken'
stderr 'broken on purpose'

# Nothing the failed run wrote reaches the module directory, and no overlay
# records the module as complete.
! exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generatedpkgs@v1.0.0/broken/broken.gen.go
! exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generatedpkgs@v1.0.0.generate

# A build that needs the module reports the same failure, rather than a missing
# symbol from a package nobody generated.
! go build ./both
stderr 'broken on purpose'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.16

require example.com/generatedpkgs v1.0.0
-- both/both.go --
package both

import (
	"example.com/generatedpkgs/one"
	"example.com/generatedpkgs/two"
)

var Names = one.Name() + two.Name()
-- usebroken/usebroken.go --
package usebroken

import "example.com/generatedpkgs/broken"

var Name = broken.Name()
-- usethree/usethree.go --
package usethree

import "example.com/generatedpkgs/three"

var Name = three.Name()
